newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, supply scarce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, supply scarce.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were mainly unchanged in late trade on Wednesday, withstanding the pressure of a drop in Treasury bonds mainly because supplies of both new and secondary issues remained fairly light.

"I'd say municipal cash prices are unchanged. There was not a lot of activity (but) there was a little sell-off in the governments. Bids might be down about one-eighth of a point but with not a lot of bonds out there, I think we're going to lag governments on the downside," a trader said.
With only a modest $1.6 billion of new municipal bond sales scheduled for this week, what offerings there were attracted sizable demand, enabling some to be repriced with lower yields.

For example, a $206 million sale by North Broward Hospital District, Florida, was repriced in the 2011 to 2027 maturities. A trader who was familiar with the deal said that the yield on the 2027 maturity was lowered to 5.75 percent from 5.78 percent.
"A couple of the smaller deals today were priced initially to draw interest, and if they were oversubscribed, they were able to lower yields by two to five basis points," another trader said.

Concerns about what the crucial unemployment data for January, which are due to be released on Friday, will reveal about the economy helped prompt at least one issuer, whose offering had been on the day-to-day calender since autumn, to pull the trigger, traders familiar with the deal said.

Wisconsin Health and Educational Facilities Authority sold about $100 million of revenue bonds, though traders said that the deal initially was priced a bit too aggressively, and later had to be repriced with a yield that was five basis points lower in the long-end at 5.90 percent. The underwriter was not immediately available to confirm the repricing.
In the secondary market, Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.66 percent, up one basis point.
And Intermountain Power Agency Utah Power Supply Revenues of July 2021, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.75 percent, NET, down one basis point.
March Treasury bond futures ended down six ticks at 112-1/32, while March municipal bond futures shed five ticks to 115-25/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 120 ticks.
